test_cases.test_name: End-to-End Workflow Template Configuration and Execution
test_cases.objective: Verify that the platform can be configured with a complete patient therapy workflow template and successfully execute it, enforcing chain-of-identity and custody.
prerequisites: System installation is complete and verified
Administrator user account with configuration privileges
Test patient and therapy product master data is loaded
Barcode scanners are connected and configured

test_steps.action: Log into the system as an administrator and navigate to the workflow template configuration module.
test_steps.expected_result: Administrator successfully authenticates and gains access to the configuration interface.

test_steps.action: Create a new workflow template defining the stages: Apheresis, Manufacturing Slot Assignment, QC Release, and Infusion.
test_steps.expected_result: System saves the new workflow template with all defined stages and configurable parameters.

test_steps.action: Initiate a new patient journey using the created template and simulate a dual-scanning event at the apheresis handoff.
test_steps.expected_result: Patient journey is created, and the system enforces dual-scanning verification before progressing the workflow.
data_to_capture: User IDs of personnel performing scans

test_steps.action: Progress the patient journey through each stage, simulating custody handoffs with dual-scans.
test_steps.expected_result: Workflow progresses correctly through each stage, and a complete audit trail is generated for all handoffs.

acceptance_criteria: Workflow template is configured and saved without errors.
Patient journey is initiated and progresses through all defined stages.
Dual-scanning verification is enforced at each handoff point.
A complete and immutable audit trail is generated for the entire journey.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records and signatures
GDP guidelines for chain-of-custody and cold-chain integrity
data_integrity_requirements: All chain-of-identity and custody events must be recorded with timestamp and user identity.
Audit trail must be immutable and capture the before-and-after state of critical data changes.
urs_requirements: URS-028-008: Full audit trail for all handoffs

test_cases.test_name: Configurable Risk Scoring and Exception Handling Workflow
test_cases.objective: Validate the configuration and execution of risk scoring rules and the associated exception handling workflow for a simulated temperature excursion event.
prerequisites: System is operational with a basic workflow template configured
User account with permissions to configure risk rules and handle exceptions
Test data for a patient journey in the logistics stage

test_steps.action: Access the risk rule configuration interface and create a rule that triggers a high-risk score if a shipment temperature exceeds 10°C.
test_steps.expected_result: The system accepts and saves the configurable risk scoring rule.

test_steps.action: Initiate a patient journey and progress it to the logistics/shipping stage.
test_steps.expected_result: Patient journey is active and in the logistics stage.

test_steps.action: Simulate a temperature excursion event by inputting a temperature reading of 12°C for the shipment.
test_steps.expected_result: The system triggers the risk rule, assigns a high-risk score, and automatically initiates the configured temperature excursion exception workflow.

test_steps.action: Follow the exception workflow steps, which should include quarantine, QA review, and an electronic signature for disposition.
test_steps.expected_result: The exception workflow guides the user through the necessary steps and requires an e-signature for the final disposition decision.

acceptance_criteria: Configurable risk rule is successfully created and activated.
Simulated temperature excursion correctly triggers the rule and initiates the exception workflow.
Exception workflow enforces the required steps and electronic signature for critical actions.
All events are recorded in the audit trail.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 for e-signatures on critical actions (disposition)
GDP guidelines for handling temperature excursions and quality decisions
data_integrity_requirements: The risk score calculation and its inputs must be recorded.
The entire exception handling process, including the e-signature, must be captured in the audit trail.
urs_requirements: URS-028-005: Support configurable risk scoring rules
URS-028-009: 21 CFR Part 11 e-signatures for critical actions
URS-028-010: Compliance with GDP for cold-chain records

test_cases.test_name: Chain-of-Identity and Chain-of-Custody Verification with Dual-Scanning
test_cases.objective: Verify the system correctly enforces chain-of-identity and chain-of-custody for patient samples and materials using dual-scanning verification at all handoff points.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured with at least one workflow template
Test users with appropriate roles (e.g., apheresis nurse, courier, manufacturing operator) are created
Barcode scanners are configured and integrated with the system
Test patient and material master data is loaded

test_steps.action: Initiate a new patient therapy workflow in the system using the configured template.
test_steps.expected_result: System creates a new patient journey with a unique identifier and initial chain-of-identity record.

test_steps.action: Simulate the apheresis collection step: scan the patient wristband and the collection kit barcode using two separate scanning devices.
test_steps.expected_result: System records a successful dual-scan event, linking the patient identity to the physical sample container. Audit trail entry is created.

test_steps.action: Simulate a handoff from apheresis to courier. Have two users (giver and receiver) scan their badges and the sample container.
test_steps.expected_result: System validates both users have correct permissions and records a custody transfer event. The chain-of-custody log is updated.

test_steps.action: Attempt an invalid handoff by scanning an incorrect user badge or mismatched barcodes.
test_steps.expected_result: System rejects the transaction, generates an error message, and logs the failed attempt in the audit trail.
data_to_capture: Audit trail entry for failed attempt

acceptance_criteria: All dual-scanning events are successfully recorded with complete metadata.
The chain-of-identity and chain-of-custody logs are accurate and immutable after each event.
Invalid handoff attempts are prevented and logged.
The audit trail contains a complete, timestamped sequence of all identity and custody events.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 - Electronic Records; Electronic Signatures
EU GDP Guidelines - Guidelines on Good Distribution Practice of medicinal products for human use
FDA Guidance on Chain of Identity and Chain of Custody for Cellular Therapy Products
data_integrity_requirements: ALCOA+ principles must be demonstrated for all identity and custody records.
Audit trail must capture the 'who, what, when, and why' for all data changes and transactions.
Records must be protected from unauthorized modification or deletion.
urs_requirements: URS-028-002: Enforce chain-of-identity and chain-of-custody with dual-scanning verification.
URS-028-008: Full audit trail for all handoffs and custody events.
URS-028-010: Compliance with GDP for logistics and cold-chain records.

test_cases.test_name: Integration with External Systems via Standard APIs
test_cases.objective: Verify the platform successfully exchanges data with external systems (EHR, LIMS, MES, Courier) using standard APIs as defined in the requirements.
prerequisites: System is installed and network connectivity is confirmed
Test instances or simulators for EHR, LIMS, MES, and a courier system are available
API credentials and endpoints for each external system are configured in the platform
Test data sets for patient, order, and shipment information are prepared

test_steps.action: Configure the connection settings in the platform for the EHR simulator. Test the connection.
test_steps.expected_result: Platform successfully establishes a connection to the EHR simulator and connection status is confirmed.

test_steps.action: From the platform, trigger a request to retrieve a patient's clinical data from the EHR simulator using a test patient ID.
test_steps.expected_result: Platform sends a correctly formatted API call and receives the expected patient data, which is displayed within the platform.

test_steps.action: Simulate a manufacturing step completion in the platform and verify it sends a status update to the MES simulator.
test_steps.expected_result: Platform automatically sends a manufacturing status message to the MES via API. MES simulator confirms receipt of the correct data.
data_to_capture: Data fields transmitted (e.g., lot number, status, timestamp)

test_steps.action: Using the platform, initiate a shipment and verify it creates a pickup request in the courier system simulator via API.
test_steps.expected_result: Courier system simulator receives a pickup request with all necessary details (pickup/drop-off locations, tracking number, temperature requirements).

test_steps.action: Simulate an API failure (e.g., disconnect the network) and attempt a data exchange. Then restore connectivity.
test_steps.expected_result: Platform detects the failure, logs an error, and implements a retry mechanism upon restoration of connectivity.
data_to_capture: Eventual successful data sync after reconnect

acceptance_criteria: The platform can successfully send and receive data from all configured external system simulators.
Data mapping between the platform and external systems is accurate and complete.
API communication failures are handled gracefully with appropriate logging and retry logic.
All integration transactions are recorded in the audit trail.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 - Requirements for systems that exchange electronic records
GAMP 5 - Good Practice Guide: Leveraging Supplier Audits for GxP Compliant Computerized Systems
data_integrity_requirements: Data transmitted via APIs must maintain integrity and accuracy.
Audit trail must record the initiation and completion of significant data exchange events.
urs_requirements: URS-028-013: Integrate with EHR, LIMS, MES, courier systems via standard APIs.
URS-028-008: Full audit trail for all handoffs and custody events.

test_cases.test_name: Performance Testing Under Maximum Concurrent Patient Load

test_steps.expected_result: Test tool successfully configured with appropriate load profile and monitoring

test_steps.action: Execute performance test run for minimum 60 minutes under maximum concurrent load
test_steps.expected_result: System remains stable and responsive throughout the test duration

test_steps.action: Measure event processing latency for critical workflow steps including scanning, status updates, and notifications
test_steps.expected_result: All event processing latencies remain below 1 second threshold

test_steps.action: Monitor system resources and identify any performance bottlenecks or degradation
test_steps.expected_result: System resources remain within acceptable limits without memory leaks or excessive CPU usage

acceptance_criteria: System maintains event processing latency < 1 second for all 1,000 concurrent journeys
No system crashes or unplanned restarts during test
All workflow events processed without data loss
Resource utilization remains within specified thresholds
regulatory_basis: FDA guidance on computerized systems in clinical trials
ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice
GAMP5 framework for performance verification
data_integrity_requirements: All performance metrics must be accurately captured and timestamped
Test results must be reproducible and verifiable
No data corruption during high-load conditions

Algorithm transparency requirements

EU MDR requirements for clinical decision support

Explainability artifacts must accurately reflect decision logic
No data corruption during algorithm processing

test_steps.action: Attempt to modify or delete any audit trail record through the system interface

acceptance_criteria: All custody events are recorded in the audit trail with complete metadata
Audit trail records are immutable and cannot be modified or deleted

21 CFR Part 211 - Current Good Manufacturing Practice
GDP Guidelines for Medicinal Products
data_integrity_requirements: ALCOA+ principles must be maintained for all audit trail records
Immutable record storage with cryptographic integrity verification
Complete metadata capture including user identity, timestamp, and action type

test_steps.expected_result: System guides user through GDP-compliant documentation process with required data capture fields

test_cases.test_name: SSO Authentication and Device Identity Verification
test_cases.objective: To verify that Single Sign-On (SSO) using OpenID Connect (OIDC) functions correctly and that device identities for scanners are properly authenticated and managed.
prerequisites: OQ-004 has been executed successfully
SSO identity provider (e.g., Azure AD, Okta) is configured and accessible
Test user accounts with appropriate roles are created in the identity provider
Barcode scanners or simulated scanner devices are available
Network connectivity to the platform and identity provider is established

test_steps.action: Attempt to access the platform login page and initiate the SSO flow by selecting the OIDC provider.
test_steps.expected_result: User is redirected to the configured OIDC identity provider's authentication page.

test_steps.action: Enter valid credentials for a test user on the identity provider's page and submit.
test_steps.expected_result: Authentication is successful, and the user is redirected back to the platform with a valid session established.

test_steps.action: Attempt to access a scanner configuration page or initiate a scanning operation requiring device authentication.
test_steps.expected_result: The platform prompts for or verifies the scanner's device identity credentials.

test_steps.action: Provide valid device credentials (e.g., certificate, API key) for a registered scanner.
test_steps.expected_result: Scanner is successfully authenticated and authorized to perform scanning operations within the platform.
data_to_capture: Authorized operations list for the device

test_steps.action: Perform a dual-scanning verification step (as defined in OQ-003) using the authenticated scanner.
test_steps.expected_result: The scanning event is recorded in the audit trail with the correct user and device identity context.
data_to_capture: Audit trail entry for the scan event
Correlation between user session and device ID

acceptance_criteria: SSO authentication via OIDC successfully grants access to authorized users only.
Device identity verification is required and successful before scanner operations are permitted.
All authentication events (user and device) are logged in the audit trail with timestamps and identifiers.
Session management prevents unauthorized access after logout or session timeout.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 - Controls for identification codes/passwords
General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) - Principles of access control
NIST Cybersecurity Framework - Identity Management and Access Control (PR.AC)
data_integrity_requirements: User and device authentication records must be immutable and timestamped.
Session tokens must be securely generated and invalidated upon logout/timeout.
Audit trails must irrevocably link actions to specific user and device identities.
urs_requirements: URS-028-014: SSO with OIDC and device identity for scanners.

test_cases.test_name: Containerized Custom Module Deployment and Version Management
test_cases.objective: To verify that optional custom-developed algorithm modules can be successfully deployed as versioned containers and integrated into the platform's workflow engine.
prerequisites: OQ-006 has been executed successfully
A container registry (e.g., Docker Hub, Azure Container Registry) is accessible
A test version of a custom algorithm module (e.g., for patient-lot matching) is built and pushed to the registry
The platform's orchestration engine (e.g., Kubernetes) is installed and configured
Platform administrative access is available for module deployment

test_steps.action: From the platform's administration interface, initiate the process to add a new custom module. Provide the container image URI and version tag from the registry.
test_steps.expected_result: Platform validates the image URI and tag, and begins pulling the container image.

test_steps.action: Configure the deployment parameters for the module, such as resource limits (CPU, memory) and environment variables required by the algorithm.
test_steps.expected_result: Platform accepts the configuration and schedules the container for deployment within the cluster.

test_steps.action: Monitor the deployment status until the module container reports a 'Ready' state.
test_steps.expected_result: Custom module container is successfully deployed, healthy, and accessible by the platform's workflow engine.

test_steps.action: Execute a test workflow (e.g., a patient journey) that is configured to invoke the newly deployed custom algorithm at a specific step.
test_steps.expected_result: The workflow executes correctly, calls the custom module via its API, and receives a valid response.

test_steps.action: Deploy a new version (v2) of the same custom module with a different image tag, without deleting v1.
test_steps.expected_result: Both v1 and v2 of the module container coexist. The platform allows workflows to be configured to use a specific version.
data_to_capture: Platform display showing multiple versions available

test_steps.action: Configure a test workflow to use v2 of the module and execute it. Then, reconfigure the workflow to use v1 and execute again.
test_steps.expected_result: Workflows execute successfully using the specified module version, demonstrating version isolation and management.
data_to_capture: Workflow results for v1 and v2

acceptance_criteria: Custom algorithm modules are successfully deployed as containers from a remote registry.
The platform manages multiple versions of the same module simultaneously.
Workflows can be configured to invoke a specific version of a custom module.
Module deployment and lifecycle operations are logged in the audit trail.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 - §11.10(a) - Validation of systems for accuracy, reliability, and consistent performance
Annex 11 - Clause 4.1 - The validation documentation should specify the sequence of and methodology for version control
data_integrity_requirements: The integrity of the container image must be verified upon pull (e.g., via checksum).
Version control must ensure that the correct, validated algorithm version is executed for a given workflow.
Deployment logs must capture the exact image digest and version tag used.
urs_requirements: URS-028-015: Custom algorithm modules shall be containerized and versioned.
URS-028-006: Allow optional custom-developed modules for patient-to-lot matching optimization.
related_tests: OQ-006: Custom Algorithm Module Integration and Explainability Verification
